basics.name: Jared A. Allen
basics.label: Critical Infrastructure Engineer | Data Center Monitoring, Controls & Physical Security
basics.summary: Hands-on infrastructure engineer with 15 years in data center operations at Liquid Web, building the hardware, software and physical security systems that keep three facilities monitored and secure. Designed custom circuit boards and deployed 10,000+ sensors of my own design, then built the web platforms, APIs and time-series monitoring that turn that data into something operations staff use every day. Pairs Linux/Windows systems administration (RHCSA) with electronics design, 3D CAD and a prior career as a Michigan State-Certified Master Automotive Technician, so I can take a problem from circuit board to dashboard to physical install.

work.name: Liquid Web (Nexcess)
work.summary: Engineer, build and run monitoring, physical security and facility systems across three data centers.
highlights: Designed and deployed 10,000+ custom 1-Wire temperature sensors across three data centers, running 700–900 sensors per bus, far beyond typical 1-Wire limits, through careful voltage tuning, noise reduction, network design and cable standards.
Redesigned RJ45 1-Wire splitters to replace a low-quality, overseas-only part, moving production to a US manufacturer and adding an onboard slot for a DS2431 address-memory chip or an extra sensor.
Designing flexible-circuit sensor strips with an onboard DS2431 that stores sensor order at manufacture, removing manual sensor mapping and replacing a commercial product with long lead times.

Deploying LoRaWAN battery sensor strings to monitor 16 GPU racks for a major customer deployment, and expanding electrical power monitoring to a new 800A panel and sub-panel through the building management system.
Built and maintain a multi-facility temperature mapping platform: each building has its own floor map and settings, with live click-through readings from every sensor and Google sign-in for staff.
Built the time-series stack behind it (InfluxDB, Prometheus, Grafana) for historical trends, plus sensor-health logging, an offline-sensor view and configurable temperature and status alerts.

Reverse engineered Foobot air quality monitors to reach the vendor API; the vendor then granted official lifetime keys. Built a scheduler and cache that spread the limited daily quota across 24 hours for continuous humidity, VOC and particulate readings on the map.

Reverse engineered Airthings Wave Mini sensors over Bluetooth LE, with Node.js collectors on Ubuntu (Raspberry Pi and Mac mini hosts). Readings feed the map and an entrance display that rotates through each aisle's conditions every 3 seconds.
Run a fleet of 27 wallboard displays across 3 facilities with Balena and Anthias, showing facility maps and critical operational data; handle deployments, updates and troubleshooting.

Designed and built a key and badge tracking system now at 3 facilities: 7 cabinets with separate permission levels track about 200 building keys, access badges and vehicle keys from one searchable web interface. Badge-in unlocks only for authorized users; iButton sockets log every removal and return. Designed the cabinets, 3D-printed key holders and software, which runs as Docker services with automatic failover.

Install and maintain access control and door hardware (badge readers, electric hinges, closers, locks, door position sensors) and IP cameras across all facilities; leading a multi-site rekey to restricted keyways, including vendor selection and purchasing.
Administer Linux and Windows servers, databases and clustered services supporting facility systems, including building management servers and the IP and industrial control networks they run on.
Patch and update Linux and Windows servers and camera NVR systems (Milestone and Wave) every month as part of infrastructure audit reports.
Design custom parts in Fusion 360 and run in-house 3D printing for data center hardware; built custom project management software to track multi-site infrastructure projects.
